structured_result.summary:
The rename looks correct, and I found no P0, P1 or P2 problems. Inside this snapshot, nothing outside the intentional compatibility code still uses the old identity. Changed: crate, imports, binary, MCP server name, skill://tosi URIs, generated plugin/tosi, archive and manifest names, and the tosi-local catalog. The five tools and the rest of the server's behaviour are unchanged by the diff.

Environment variables: config::lookup only falls back to TASK_RUNNERS_* when the TOSI_* name is unset. An empty, invalid or non-UTF-8 TOSI_* value stays in force and causes the error it should. Binary paths are passed through as OsString without loss.

Nested-server protection: either TOSI_CHILD=1 or TASK_RUNNERS_CHILD=1 blocks startup, whatever the other variable says. Both workers set both markers, so old and new servers block each other in both directions. Doctor is still not blocked inside a worker. Paid live tests still need an explicit opt-in; an empty or 0 TOSI_LIVE_TESTS does not fall back to the old name.

I have three minor (P3) items: error messages that name only the TOSI_* variable, missing migration steps for the old local catalog, and a few gaps in the tests.

findings.title: Startup errors name TOSI_* even when the bad value came from the old TASK_RUNNERS_* variable
findings.scenario: An existing setup has TASK_RUNNERS_DEFAULT_BACKEND=Codex (or a bad TASK_RUNNERS_MAX_CONCURRENCY) and no TOSI_* variable. config::var falls back to the old value, which fails, and startup reports "TOSI_DEFAULT_BACKEND must be claude or codex" (or "TOSI_MAX_CONCURRENCY must be between 1 and 32").
findings.evidence: main.rs:71-83 always names TOSI_* in the error text. config::var does not record which name supplied the value. A non-numeric MAX_CONCURRENCY goes through `value.parse()?` and gives a bare ParseIntError that names no variable (this last part is older behaviour).
findings.impact: Not a safety problem: startup still fails as it should. But someone migrating is sent to a variable they never set, so the misconfiguration takes longer to find.
findings.suggested_correction: Have config return the name that supplied the value (for example `Option<(String, OsString)>`), or mention both names in the message, e.g. "TOSI_DEFAULT_BACKEND (or legacy TASK_RUNNERS_DEFAULT_BACKEND) must be claude or codex". Optionally give the same treatment to the parse error.

findings.title: Migration steps don't cover removing the old task-runners-local catalog that pointed at the old directory
findings.scenario: On each of the two machines, the old catalog task-runners-local was added from /…/task-runners. The source directory has now moved to /…/tosi. The user follows the migration section, adds tosi-local and removes the old plugin, but the task-runners-local catalog is still registered and points at a path that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: README.md:110-118 says to install tosi@tosi-local and to "remove or disable the old Task Runners installation". It never mentions removing the old task-runners-local catalog registration. The install commands at lines 71-85 only add catalogs.
findings.impact: Host catalog refreshes may show errors or stale entries for a path that no longer exists. If the old plugin's cached binary is still enabled, both servers could load the same five tools.
findings.suggested_correction: Add one sentence plus the commands each host uses to uninstall task-runners@task-runners-local and remove the task-runners-local catalog, before or after adding tosi-local.

findings.title: Some compatibility tests can pass for the wrong reason or test only a helper
findings.scenario: Three gaps: (1) empty_or_invalid_primary_settings_do_not_fall_back_to_legacy_values only checks that startup failed, not why. (2) Live-test gating is tested through config::lookup with injected closures, not through the actual enabled() function in tests/live.rs. (3) No test checks that `tosi doctor` still runs with TOSI_CHILD=1 or TASK_RUNNERS_CHILD=1 set.
findings.evidence: shutdown.rs:309-327 asserts only `!output.status.success()`. config.rs:686-705 calls lookup(), not live.rs enabled(). No test in tests/diagnostics.rs sets either CHILD variable for the doctor command.
findings.impact: If a later change makes startup fail for an unrelated reason, or makes doctor obey the nested-server block, these tests would not notice. Today's code behaves correctly when read.
findings.suggested_correction: Check stderr for the expected TOSI_DEFAULT_BACKEND / TOSI_MAX_CONCURRENCY message. Add a doctor test with TOSI_CHILD=1 (and one with TASK_RUNNERS_CHILD=1) that expects ready=true with a fake provider. Optionally move the live-gating decision into a pure function that takes a lookup closure and test it directly.

coverage: The whole of CHANGES.diff (1568 lines), plus AGENTS.md, README.md (install and migration sections), Cargo.toml and .gitignore

src/config.rs, src/main.rs (startup block for workers, default backend and concurrency settings, doctor path), src/backend.rs (binary overrides, CHILD markers on both workers, error messages), src/diagnostics.rs (which environment variables doctor reports)
xtask/src/main.rs: package metadata, release-build artifact selection, plugin/manifest/MCP launch command generation, both catalogs, archive naming and layout

tests/shutdown.rs (precedence, startup block, invalid-value tests), tests/backend.rs (both markers passed to workers), tests/diagnostics.rs (legacy binary-override test), tests/live.rs gating, tests/resources.rs, tests/support/mod.rs

A case-insensitive grep for any leftover task-runners / task_runners / TASK_RUNNERS outside the diff: the only hits are the intended compatibility code and docs, plus a generic phrase "existing task runners" at ROADMAP.md:224
The rules for old/new interoperation in both directions, and that paid live tests stay opt-in when TOSI_LIVE_TESTS is empty or 0
limitations: This was a source-only review. I did not run any tests, builds or scripts; I relied on the test results you supplied.

I reviewed only this source copy. I could not inspect the renamed candidate binary, the generated plugin/tosi package or the archives, so I could not check that the installed runtime matches this source.
I could not confirm the source-directory move from task-runners to tosi beyond what the docs say, because the copy is in a temporary directory with a different name.
I only judged host-side marketplace and cache behaviour (Codex and Claude Code plugin management) from the README; I did not verify it.
No paid live provider runs were done for this rename, so real nested-server blocking inside actual Claude and Codex workers was checked only by reading the code and the fake-provider tests.
This review was run on the original installed Task Runners server, not the renamed one.
